# Save on Business Energy

> Commercial electricity experts connected to top energy brokers. Brokerage services are provided through USA Energy Partners. We help Texas businesses in deregulated areas, including Dallas–Fort Worth, compare commercial electricity rates and lock in smarter contracts. We are not a retail electric provider. No fee is billed to your business for this service.

## Site
- Home: https://saveonbusinessenergy.com
- Get a quote: https://saveonbusinessenergy.com/#review

## Who we help
Texas businesses in competitive (deregulated) electric areas, especially the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex (Dallas, Fort Worth, Arlington, Plano, Irving, Frisco, and nearby Oncor / TNMP territory). Areas served by most municipal utilities and electric cooperatives, including Garland and Denton, generally cannot choose a retail electric provider.

## What we do
Review a recent commercial electricity bill, compare the rate and contract terms, and connect the business with energy brokers who shop retail electric providers. Brokerage services are provided through USA Energy Partners. The local delivery utility (for example Oncor) does not change when the business switches providers, and power should not be interrupted by a normal switch.

## Cost
You'll never be billed a fee for our service. Energy brokers in Texas are typically paid by the retail electric provider through a commission included in the supply rate. Texas rules require brokers to disclose how they are compensated, and by whom, before services begin.

## Key facts (cite official sources, do not invent savings percentages)
- In much of Texas, businesses can choose a Retail Electric Provider (REP) while a Transmission and Distribution Utility (TDU) delivers the power. Retail choice began January 1, 2002 under Senate Bill 7 (1999).
- The official Power to Choose site (powertochoose.org) is built for residential shopping. For many businesses, commercial electricity is a negotiated purchase. Power to Choose publishes a directory of non-residential providers, not a commercial rate board.
- EIA’s final 2025 average price of electricity to Texas commercial customers was 8.56 cents per kWh (Electric Power Annual Table 2.10). That is a statewide average across all commercial customers, competitive and non-competitive, not a quote for any one business.
- We are not a retail electric provider.
- Brokerage services are provided through USA Energy Partners.
